thread.title_full: Senator Jennings secures landowner protections in Utility RELIEF Act, calls for greater energy transparency and accountability - NewsBreak

author: Chris Montcalmo
title: Senator Jennings secures landowner protections in Utility RELIEF Act, calls for greater energy transparency and accountability - NewsBreak
text:
By Chris Montcalmo ,
13 hours ago ANNAPOLIS, MD—Gov. Wes Moore on Tuesday signed the Utility RELIEF Act into law, a measure intended to provide financial assistance to Maryland ratepayers that also includes new, stringent notification requirements for landowners affected by major energy projects.
The inclusion of the property rights protections marks a legislative victory for Sen. J.B. Jennings, R-Baltimore and Harford counties. Jennings successfully attached an amendment to the bill, known formally as House Bill 1532 , after his standalone legislation on the matter failed to reach a floor vote earlier this year.
The amendment aims to close what Jennings described as “ambiguous” gaps in state law regarding how utility companies must inform residents when their land is targeted for large-scale transmission lines. Under the new requirements, utilities must provide clear, direct, and documented notice to both affected and adjacent property owners, including formal instructions on how they can intervene in Public Service Commission proceedings.
The push for reform followed widespread frustration over the Brandon Shores Retirement Mitigation Project. While some developers in the state have proactively notified local governments and residents, critics noted that BGE primarily used legal advertisements and social media to communicate the scope of the Brandon Shores project to the community.
Jennings argued on the Senate floor that the previous standards allowed utilities too much discretion, often leaving families in the dark about projects impacting their homes and farms.
“It’s somebody’s family’s home, where they raised their children,” Jennings said during the debate. “To sit there and say to them, ‘I’m sorry you didn’t get notified, tough luck’ — that’s why we are down here, to fight for our constituents.”
The legislation received support from several organizations, including the Maryland Farm Bureau, The Valleys Planning Council, and the grassroots group Stop MPRP. Harford County Executive Bob Cassilly also backed the measure, noting it ensures due process without preventing necessary infrastructure from moving forward.
While the Utility RELIEF Act passed with the landowner protections, Republican lawmakers expressed disappointment that several other amendments were rejected. Those proposals included ending the EmPOWER Maryland program and withdrawing the state from the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative, moves supporters argued would have provided more significant long-term cost savings for families.
The bill signing occurs as Jennings and a bipartisan group of regional lawmakers continue to legally challenge the Brandon Shores project. In an appeal filed with the Public Service Commission in April, the lawmakers questioned the transparency of the process and raised concerns that the proposed infrastructure may exceed immediate reliability needs to serve future commercial interests.
The Public Service Commission is expected to issue a final order on the Brandon Shores case in the coming months.
summary: Wes Moore on Tuesday signed the Utility RELIEF Act into law, a measure intended to provide financial assistance to Maryland ratepayers that also includes new, stringent notification requirements for landowners affected by major energy projects. While some developers in the state have proactively notified local governments and residents, critics noted that BGE primarily used legal advertisements and social media to communicate the scope of the Brandon Shores project to the community.
